newsitem.title: LEBANON: Group seeks release of Lebanese journalist.
newsitem.headline: Group seeks release of Lebanese journalist.

text.p: An international press freedom watchdog group appealed on Wednesday to Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri to help obtain the release of a television journalist charged with collaborating with Israel.

In an open letter faxed to an international news agency in Beirut, Paris-based Reporters sans Frontieres (Reporters without Frontiers) asked Hariri to use his influence to obtain clarification of the charges against Tony Chamie of the privately owned Murr TV.
Chamie, 38, was editor of the station's daily news programme before his arrest in March.

A military investigating judge charged him and six other men on March 14 with "contacting the Israeli enemy and its agents, giving the enemy information and plotting against Lebanon". The charge carries a 10-year jail sentence.
Reporters sans Frontieres said Chamie was being held at Roumie prison near Beirut but no official information was available about his case.

"Reporters sans Frontieres asks you to use all your influence so that the charges against Tony Chamie are specified and that he is immediately released if his arrest is connected with his journalistic activity or his political opinions," the letter to Hariri said.
